attack_mechanism: Probing `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_dmem_addr` during that transaction exposes R4 directly for a move/store or reveals a deterministic address/data function of R4. An instruction that uses R4 as a source operand, store datum, or address base transfers its contents from the register file into the memory address/data backbone. `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_dmem_addr` carries the resulting address, data word, or bus-selected derivative when the implementation qualifies this propagation with `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`. The relevant internal route is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.op_src_inv -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add -> openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_dmem_addr`. The observation discloses all or part of the confidential R4 value and repeated chosen instructions can resolve otherwise masked bits.

Observing `openMSP430.per_dout_sfr` while a chosen peripheral transaction consumes R4 exposes a value correlated with the register contents. Across selected operands or repeated transactions, that correlation discloses R4 bits outside the protected register file.
